specs.title: NUT-00: Notation, Utilization, and Terminology
specs.summary: The notation, models and cryptography the rest of the specification is written in: blinding, signing, proofs, and how a token is serialised.

specs.title: NUT-01: Mint public key exchange
specs.summary: How a wallet fetches a mint's active public keys, one per amount, and what a keyset is.

specs.title: NUT-02: Keysets and fees
specs.summary: Keysets: how an id is derived from one, how a mint rotates them, and the input fee a wallet pays when spending ecash from one.

specs.title: NUT-03: Swap tokens
specs.summary: The swap operation, where a wallet hands proofs to the mint and receives new blind signatures in return.

specs.title: NUT-04: Mint tokens
specs.summary: Minting: the two-step flow where a wallet requests a quote, pays it, and then asks the mint to issue ecash.

specs.title: NUT-05: Melting tokens
specs.summary: Melting: the two-step flow where a wallet asks the mint to pay a request and spends ecash to cover it.

specs.title: NUT-06: Mint information
specs.summary: The info endpoint, where a mint declares its name, its keys, its contacts, and which NUTs it supports.

specs.title: NUT-07: Token state check
specs.summary: How a wallet asks the mint whether a proof is unspent, pending, or already spent.

specs.title: NUT-08: Lightning fee return
specs.summary: Blank outputs, which let a mint return the Lightning fees a wallet overpaid when melting.

specs.title: NUT-09: Restore signatures
specs.summary: How a wallet asks the mint to reissue blind signatures it once received, so a lost wallet can be restored.

specs.title: NUT-10: Spending conditions
specs.summary: The well-known secret format that turns a proof's secret into a spending condition the mint enforces.

specs.title: NUT-11: Pay to Public Key (P2PK)
specs.summary: Locking ecash to a public key, redeemable only against a Schnorr signature from the key that owns it.

specs.title: NUT-12: Offline ecash signature validation
specs.summary: DLEQ proofs, which let anyone verify a mint's signature offline with nothing but its public keys.

specs.title: NUT-13: Deterministic Secrets
specs.summary: Secrets derived from a seed phrase, so a wallet can regenerate its ecash after losing the device that held it.

specs.title: NUT-14: Hashed Timelock Contracts (HTLCs)
specs.summary: Ecash locked to the hash of a preimage and a deadline, which makes atomic swaps between users possible.

specs.title: NUT-15: Partial multi-path payments
specs.summary: Paying one Lightning invoice from several mints at once, all of them or none.

specs.title: NUT-16: Animated QR codes
specs.summary: How to show a token too large for a static QR code as an animated one, using the UR protocol.

specs.title: NUT-17: WebSockets
specs.summary: A JSON-RPC WebSocket protocol for subscribing to quote and proof state changes instead of polling for them.

specs.title: NUT-18: Payment Requests
specs.summary: A request format carrying everything a sending wallet needs, so a transaction can be started by whoever is being paid.

specs.title: NUT-19: Cached Responses
specs.summary: Response caching on the critical endpoints, so a wallet can safely replay a request that a network error interrupted.

specs.title: NUT-20: Signature on Mint Quote
specs.summary: Binding a mint quote to a public key, so only the holder of the matching secret key can redeem it.

specs.title: NUT-21: Clear Authentication
specs.summary: How a mint restricts its endpoints to users holding a token from an OpenID Connect service it trusts.

specs.title: NUT-22: Blind Authentication
specs.summary: Blind authentication tokens, which let a mint restrict access to registered users without learning which one is calling.

specs.title: NUT-23: BOLT11
specs.summary: Minting and melting with bolt11 Lightning invoices, the method specifics on top of the shared mint and melt flows.

specs.title: NUT-24: HTTP 402 Payment Required
specs.summary: How an HTTP server demands payment with a 402 response carrying a Cashu payment request.

specs.title: NUT-25: BOLT12
specs.summary: Minting and melting with bolt12 Lightning offers.

specs.title: NUT-26: Payment Request Bech32m Encoding
specs.summary: A bech32m encoding of payment requests, smaller than the CBOR form and friendlier to QR codes.

specs.title: NUT-27: Nostr Mint Backup
specs.summary: How a wallet backs up its mint list to Nostr relays, encrypted under keys derived from its own seed phrase.

specs.title: NUT-28: Pay to Blinded Key (P2BK)
specs.summary: Blinding the receiver's public key on each payment, so the mint cannot link several of them to the same person.

specs.title: NUT-29: Batched Minting
specs.summary: Minting several quotes in one atomic request.

specs.title: NUT-30: Payment Method: Onchain
specs.summary: Minting and melting with onchain Bitcoin payments.
